items.explanation: All four parts are grammatically correct.
With neither/nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'assistants', so 'were' is needed.
'Despite' is not followed by 'of'; the phrase should be 'despite the fact that' or 'in spite of the fact that'.

sentences: The manager, along with his team, is attending the conference this week.
The manager, along with his team, are attending the conference this week.
The manager, along with his team, were attending the conference this week.
The manager, along with his team, attend the conference this week.
The manager, along with his team, be attending the conference this week.
items.explanation: The subject is the singular 'manager'; 'along with his team' does not make it plural, so 'is' is correct.
